key_insight: Cortical thinning in dementia with Lewy bodies appears linked to both shared neurodegenerative biology (mitochondrial, synaptic, Parkinson’s/Alzheimer’s pathways) and DLB-specific GABA-related and network features.
clinical_relevance: These findings may help explain why some brain regions are selectively vulnerable in DLB and could guide future biomarker and target discovery, but they are not yet directly actionable in routine care.
method: 89 DLB patients and 89 matched controls underwent T1-weighted MRI with surface-based cortical thickness mapping.
Regional thinning patterns were linked to postmortem human brain gene-expression data to identify molecular signatures.
Spatial mapping tested overlap with neurotransmitter systems and structural connectivity networks.
evidence_signal: The study integrated MRI from 178 participants with transcriptomic and spatial mapping analyses, finding overlap with Parkinson’s and Alzheimer’s pathways plus 90 DLB-associated genes enriched for GABAergic signalling.
watch_item: The gene-expression and neurotransmitter findings are associative and based on healthy reference datasets, so they do not prove causality or immediate treatment targets.
paper_title: Selective Molecular and Network Architecture Features Underlie Brain Cortical Atrophy in Dementia with Lewy Bodies
